title: New ranking shows Texas as the most ghost-sighting state
excerpt: A new study by search-data company Answer Socrates revealed that Texas has logged the highest number of ghost sightings in the nation at 7,669, despite ranking seventh overall in haunting intensity…
content:
DALLAS (KDAF) — Texas has logged 7,669 ghost sightings, the most of any state in the nation, according to a new ranking released by search-data company Answer Socrates ahead of Halloween this Saturday.

Overall, Texas ranks as the seventh most haunted state in America with a haunt score of 68 out of 100.

The study evaluated all 50 states across nine public records and 12 months of Google Trends search data. By raw totals, Texas ranks as the second most ghostly state in the country, supported by thousands of reported sightings, hundreds of haunted locations and thousands of historic sites.

Among Texas municipalities, El Paso leads the state in reader-reported ghost sightings on Ghosts of America with 197 reports. Austin follows with 115 sightings, Corpus Christi with 105, Laredo with 103 and Midland with 82.

On the Shadowlands index, Texas contains 696 reportedly haunted locations, placing second nationwide. San Antonio tops all Texas cities with 55 haunted locations, followed by El Paso with 37, Houston with 33, Laredo with 32 and Austin with 21.

The state features 6,990 cemeteries, ranking fifth nationally, along with 591 ghost towns, which ranks seventh. Texas also holds 3,596 historic places, placing fifth and 210 spooky place names, ranking sixth. Spooky place names in the state include Big Devil Bayou, Coffin Mountain and Dead Mans Hole.

Additionally, Texas has recorded 4,170 UFO reports, ranking fourth in the nation by total volume, though it represents the fewest reports per person of any state. Online search patterns show a distinct trend among Texas residents. While Texas ranks 42nd of 50 states for Google searches regarding haunted places and 40th for ghosts, it ranks second nationwide for searches involving the chupacabra and fourth for the Goatman. Google autocompletes the query “why is texas so haunted” with Galveston, Austin and Jefferson as top locations.

James Oliver, founder of Socrates, noted the unique search patterns of Texas residents. “Texans seem more interested in the monsters than the ghosts,” Oliver said. “They searching the Goatman and chupacabra, but much lower for ghosts and haunted places. Maybe in Texas, the things lurking in the woods get more attention than the ones lurking in the old houses.”

Socrates compiled the ranking by combining public records and Google Trends search volume over the past 12 months. Public records analyzed included reports from the Shadowlands Haunted Places Index, Ghosts of America, the USGS Geographic Names Information System, the National Register of Historic Places, the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization and the National UFO Reporting Center. Each state was evaluated on raw counts and per 100,000 residents, with the final haunt score calculated as the average of three group scores: Ghostly, Mysterious and Ghost-obsessed.

All facts in this report were gathered by journalists employed by CW33. Artificial intelligence tools were used to reformat information into a news article for our website. This report was edited and fact-checked by CW33 staff before being published.
